Iterating, $\eta_n = \Sigma^{n-2}(\eta_2)$, so $\eta_n$ is an iterated suspension. The group $\pi_{n+1}(S^n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$ is generated by $\eta_n$.

**Key fact: suspended maps are co-H-maps.** The comultiplication (pinch map) $c_{\Sigma X}: \Sigma X \to \Sigma X \vee \Sigma X$ is natural with respect to suspended maps: if $\beta: A \to B$, then $c_{\Sigma B} \circ \Sigma\beta = (\Sigma\beta \vee \Sigma\beta) \circ c_{\Sigma A}$. Since $\eta_n = \Sigma(\eta_{n-1})$ is a suspension, it is a co-H-map:
$$c_{S^n} \circ \eta_n = (\eta_n \vee \eta_n) \circ c_{S^{n+1}}.$$

**Composition is additive in the first variable.** The group law on $[S^n, S^n] \cong \pi_n(S^n)$ uses the co-H structure on $S^n$ (the source), and the group law on $[S^{n+1}, S^n] \cong \pi_{n+1}(S^n)$ uses the co-H structure on $S^{n+1}$. For $f, g \in [S^n, S^n]$ and $\alpha = \eta_n$:
$$(f + g) \circ \alpha = \nabla \circ (f \vee g) \circ c_{S^n} \circ \alpha = \nabla \circ (f \vee g) \circ (\alpha \vee \alpha) \circ c_{S^{n+1}} = \nabla \circ (f\circ\alpha \vee g\circ\alpha) \circ c_{S^{n+1}} = f\circ\alpha + g\circ\alpha,$$
where the second equality uses that $\alpha$ is a co-H-map, and $\nabla$ is the fold map. Thus pre-composition by $\alpha$ is a group homomorphism $[S^n, S^n] \to [S^{n+1}, S^n]$.

**Reducing mod 2.** Since $\pi_{n+1}(S^n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$, the element $m \cdot \eta_n$ depends only on $m \pmod{2}$:

$$\boxed{(\delta_m^{(n)})_*(\eta_n) = m \cdot \eta_n = \begin{cases} \eta_n & \text{if } m \text{ is odd}, \\ 0 & \text{if } m \text{ is even}. \end{cases}}$$

**Independent verification via the cofiber sequence.** Consider the cofiber sequence $S^n \xrightarrow{\delta_m} S^n \to M(\mathbb{Z}/m, n)$. The long exact sequence in homotopy gives:
$$\pi_{n+1}(S^n) \xrightarrow{(\delta_m)_*} \pi_{n+1}(S^n) \to \pi_{n+1}(M) \to \pi_n(S^n) \xrightarrow{\times m} \pi_n(S^n).$$

This is $0$ when $m$ is odd (so $(\delta_m)_*$ is surjective, hence the identity on $\mathbb{Z}/2$) and $\mathbb{Z}/2$ when $m$ is even (so $(\delta_m)_* = 0$), confirming the result.
